```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(emss)
options(width = 90, digits = 4)
```

The ESS cut scores are a recommendation. A policy body may adjust them: to
make cuts progress smoothly across grades, to adopt the panelists' median
instead of the modal cut, or to try a proposed value. `update()` replaces
the modal cut scores of one or more units with values you give, and
recomputes everything that depends on them. You can then compare the
consistency and impact of the manual cuts with those of the estimated ones.

The notation follows [How embedded standard setting works](ess-method.html).

# The study

The simulated study from [Getting started](getting-started.html): three
grades, two tables of four panelists, 40 items per grade, and three levels.

```{r}
#| label: fit
set.seed(7)
sim <- generateMockDataSet(ngca = 3, ntable = 2, npanelist = 4, cor_val = 0.7, nlevel = 3,
                      sdinp = 1, ecinp = 0, n = 40, 300, 500,
                      domains = c("Number", "Algebra", "Geometry"))
res <- emstans(data = sim, location = "Loc_RP50")
res
```

The Level3 cut barely rises from M1 to M2 (`r extract(res, "cutscore")[["M1-All"]][2]`
and `r extract(res, "cutscore")[["M2-All"]][2]`) and then jumps for M3
(`r extract(res, "cutscore")[["M3-All"]][2]`). A committee might prefer a
smoother progression, with the M2 cut halfway between M1 and M3.

# Using `update()`

Give one numeric vector per unit, named as in `extract(res, "cutscore")`,
with one cut score per cut level, in increasing order:

```{r}
#| label: update
mid <- mean(c(extract(res, "cutscore")[["M1-All"]][2], extract(res, "cutscore")[["M3-All"]][2]))
mid
res_man <- update(res, `M2-All` = c(366.6, mid))
res_man
```

Several units can be updated in one call, in any order. Each unit needs
exactly $K - 1$ values. A unit name that doesn't exist, the wrong number of
values, or a cut above every item location is an error. To go back to the
estimated cuts, use the original object or run `emstans()` again.

# What is recomputed

For a unit with manual cuts $\tilde c_2, \dots, \tilde c_K$:

1. **Pages.** Each cut is placed before the first item at or above it:
   $\tilde p_k = \min\{\, p : b_{(p)} \ge \tilde c_k \,\}$.
2. **Count and Weight.** Both are evaluated at the cut score itself,
   $C_k(\tilde c_k)$ and $W_k(\tilde c_k)$. The count equals that of page
   $\tilde p_k$, because no item lies between $b_{(\tilde p_k - 1)}$ and
   $\tilde c_k$. The weight is lower than at $b_{(\tilde p_k)}$ whenever the
   profile is still falling there, since $W_k$ is linear between item
   locations with slope $(p - n_{<k})/\sigma$ after page $p$:
   $$
   W_k(\tilde c_k) = W_k\big(b_{(\tilde p_k)}\big) - \frac{(\tilde p_k - 1 - n_{<k})\,\big(b_{(\tilde p_k)} - \tilde c_k\big)}{\sigma}.
   $$
3. **Empirical levels** $o_i = 1 + \#\{\, k : \tilde c_k \le b_i \,\}$,
   and from them the agreement, the crosstabs, the item review and the
   impact data.

The panelist cuts, the per-table modal cuts, the median and average cuts,
and the inconsistency profiles stay as estimated. They describe the
panelists' judgements, which a manual cut does not change.

```{r}
#| label: recomputed
modal_all <- function(x, unit) {
  m <- x$modal[x$modal$unit == unit & x$modal$table == "All", ]
  m[, c("level", "page", "cut_score", "count", "weight")]
}
modal_all(res, "M2-All")
modal_all(res_man, "M2-All")
```

The manual Level3 cut lies between two items. Its weight is below the weight
at the next item's location, as the formula in step 2 says:

```{r}
#| label: weight-formula
u <- res$units[["M2-All"]]
a <- res$modal_items$aligned[res$modal_items$unit == "M2-All"]
p <- which(u$location >= mid)[1]
prof <- extract(res, "profile")[["M2-All"]]
prof[p, "Level3 weight"] - (p - 1 - sum(a < 3)) * (u$location[p] - mid) / u$sd
```

# The cost of a manual cut

The estimated cut minimizes the chosen criterion, so for the same criterion
a manual cut can only add inconsistency:

$$
\Delta W_k = W_k(\tilde c_k) - W_k(\hat c_k) \ge 0,
\qquad
\Delta C_k = C_k(\tilde c_k) - C_k(\hat c_k) \ge 0
$$

under ESS-Weight and ESS-Count respectively. The other criterion can move
either way. Here the manual Level3 cut has a larger weight, which ESS-Weight
minimizes, but a smaller count:

```{r}
#| label: cost
cbind(estimated = modal_all(res, "M2-All")[2, c("count", "weight")],
      manual    = modal_all(res_man, "M2-All")[2, c("count", "weight")])
```

The profile plot marks the manual cut on the profile:

```{r}
#| label: plot
plot(res_man, "profile", unit = "M2-All")
```

Because the cuts are ordered, the counts add up to the total level
disagreement, $\sum_k C_k(\tilde c_k) = \sum_i \lvert a_i - o_i \rvert$ (see
[What the minimum values add up to](ess-method.html#sec-totals)). Fewer
inconsistent items therefore means higher agreement:

```{r}
#| label: agreement
ag <- function(x) {
  s <- extract(x, "detailed")$agreement
  s[s$unit == "M2-All" & s$type == "exact", c("agree", "disagree", "weighted_kappa")]
}
rbind(estimated = ag(res), manual = ag(res_man))
```

This is not a contradiction. ESS-Weight puts the cut so that the number of
items below it matches the number aligned below the level, which need not
minimize the number of misplaced items (see [ESS-Weight is a quantile of
the item locations](ess-method.html#sec-quantile)).

# Impact and item review

Impact changes only for the levels on either side of the changed cut:

```{r}
#| label: impact
imp <- function(x) {
  s <- extract(x, "summary")
  s[s$unit == "M2-All", c("level", "page_from", "page_to", "cut_score", "pct_in", "pct_at_above")]
}
imp(res)
imp(res_man)
```

The item review lists the items that the manual cuts place outside their
aligned level:

```{r}
#| label: review
rv <- extract(res_man, "review")
rv[rv$unit == "M2-All" & rv$status != "Consistent",
   c("item_id", "page", "aligned", "operational", "location", "distance", "status")]
```

`report(res_man)` shows all of this in the HTML report, with the manual units
named in its header.

# Another common choice: the panelists' median

Instead of the modal cut, a committee may adopt the median of the panelists'
cuts:

```{r}
#| label: median
md <- extract(res, "individual")$median
md <- md[md$table == "All", ]
med_cuts <- split(md$cut_score, md$unit)
med_cuts
res_med <- do.call(update, c(list(res), med_cuts))
summary(res_med)
```

Here the modal and median columns show the same values, because the modal
cuts were replaced by the medians.
